Date: 2025-08-23 | Start: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 47m
Redwood: Samir Patel (AE), Lucia Gomez (SE) | Silverpine: Evan Lee (Eng Mgr), Priya Singh (ML Eng), Darla Moss (Product)
summary: Intro/demo of Redwood hosted Chat/Text generation (streaming behavior, key params, retry/backoff patterns). Discussed cost vs latency trade-offs, console Optimize suggestions, and edge-case handling (truncated streams, idempotency). Agreed to run a 1-week pilot and exchange security docs and benchmark scripts.
topics: console: Optimize suggestions and batching advice
hosting options: hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC concerns
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Samir from Redwood, i'll kick off. um quick intro — lucia our solutions engineer is here.
[00:11] Evan: hi, thanks, excited. we have a pretty tight timeline, want to ship a chat assistant into the product in q4.
[00:18] Priya: yeah we've got latency targets ~250ms p50, and cost budget is, well, low.
[00:25] Lucia: cool, we'll show how streaming helps latency while Optimize can help with cost suggestions — also we'll demo console recommendations.
[00:33] Darla: and security — we need SOC2 + SSO, also curious about data residency.
[00:40] Samir: noted, we'll cover security at the end and i'll send the docs. ok first, quick demo of a hosted chat request.
[00:49] Lucia: (screen) sending a streaming chat call now, note the stream chunks arrive as tokens as they're generated, so you see partial replies quickly.
[01:05] Priya: is that websocket or SSE under the hood?
[01:09] Lucia: we use server-sent events over HTTPS for the streaming endpoint by default, websockets are supported in some SDKs. sometimes transcript shows websocket, but it's sse actually.
[01:21] Evan: if the stream cuts mid-sentence, how do you recommend recovering?
[01:25] Lucia: great question — two patterns: client-side re-request with last-confirmed token id, or rely on our idempotency key and resume semantics. we don't currently have a byte-range resume for the token stream but we provide good error codes and recommended reconcat.
[01:41] Samir: also prefix caching (kv cache) helps — if you're re-requesting same conversation prefix, the token generation is fast and cheaper.
[01:50] Priya: you said KV cash?
[01:52] Lucia: sorry — kv cache, yes — the internal cache of token prefixes. sometimes the transcript spells it cash, weird.
[02:00] Darla: what about parameters — temp, top_p, max_tokens — what's the default and your recommendation?
[02:06] Lucia: defaults: temperature 0.0-0.2 for deterministic dialogs, top_p 0.95, max_tokens you control. for assistant with follow-ups we suggest 0.0-0.3, and using stop sequences to avoid runaway tokens.
[02:20] Priya: if we lower temperature and use beam-ish configs, will we lose helpfulness?
[02:24] Samir: typically lower temp + better prompts and system instructions give more stable outputs. Optimize can run A/B sets against your prompt corpus and recommend sweet spots.
[02:36] Evan: can Optimize suggest quantization or model variants?
[02:40] Lucia: yes — console Optimize suggests model variants (smaller quantized version) and quantization profiles for throughput/cost tradeoffs; it shows estimated cost/token and latency percentiles from similar workloads.
[02:56] Darla: show us a failure mode — e.g., high latency tail on long context?
[03:02] Lucia: okay i’ll simulate long context — sending a 6k token prompt. watch the console — kernel selection jumps to a different exec path and latency spikes at tail. you see a chart showing p95 jump.
[03:20] Priya: how do we keep p95 down?
[03:23] Lucia: options: truncate or summarize long context, enable prefix caching for reused prompts, or route long-context requests to Dedicated with larger batch windows. smart routing can fallback to cheaper variant if latency SLO violated.
[03:38] Samir: and autoscaler can be tuned — for spiky workloads use burst capacity.
[03:44] Evan: what's the unit economics difference Hosted vs Dedicated?
[03:48] Samir: rough rule: hosted is pay-as-you-go at token unit pricing; Dedicated reduces per-token compute cost for steady heavy throughput but has monthly commit. we'll send a pricing range.
[03:58] Darla: what about retries — we worry about duplicate actions in downstream systems.
[04:02] Lucia: retries should be idempotent — include an idempotency key at request time. for chat generation, we recommend client-side dedupe by message id; for side-effects, have the application confirm before applying.
[04:19] Priya: any recommended backoff pattern?
[04:21] Lucia: exponential backoff with jitter, typical pattern: initial 100-200ms, double each retry up to a few seconds, 3 retries max. also for streaming we recommend reconnect+resume approach w/ idempotency keys.
[04:39] Evan: is there a server-side retry that we should be aware of?
[04:42] Samir: the platform has automatic transient retries for infra failures; you can set timeouts and our SDK surfaces retryable flag.
[04:50] Darla: how accurate are your latency numbers, and can we get token-level breakdowns?
[04:55] Lucia: console -> per-token breakdown, model time vs queue time vs network. Optimize shows token cost breakouts too.
[05:06] Evan: can Optimize simulate costs for our expected qps?
[05:09] Lucia: yes upload sample traffic and Optimize will estimate monthly cost under different configs.
[05:14] Priya: about security, if we choose hosted, will our data be stored?
[05:19] Samir: host option allows configurable retention; we support short retention and encryption-at-rest with KMS. for strict data residency we offer Private (VPC/on-prem) installs.
[05:32] Darla: SSO?
[05:33] Samir: SAML/Okta yes, RBAC in console. audit logs available in Dedicated/Private and as an add-on for hosted.
[05:41] Priya: ok, show the console Optimize tab again — curious about suggested batching rules.
[05:47] Lucia: (screen) Optimize suggests batching windows per latency SLO; e.g., for p50 150ms we advise 2-4ms batching only for background ops, but for interactive chat we keep batch small to avoid latency. it also suggests prefix caching for repeated system prompts.
[06:09] Evan: if we enable batching, will ordering be affected for concurrent sessions?
[06:13] Lucia: no — we keep session isolation; batching combines independent tokens in the runtime but associates outputs back to request ids. there is added queueing delay but not reordering.
[06:22] Priya: what about streaming partial outputs when batching?
[06:25] Lucia: partial outputs may be buffered until the first token is available — you might see slightly later first-byte but subsequent tokens stream normally. we surface those tradeoffs in Optimize.
[06:38] Darla: any gotchas with stop sequences if stream interrupted?
[06:41] Lucia: if stream interrupts before stop token, client should re-request with conversation context; our guidance is to treat generation as append-only and rely on idempotency/id-based recompute.
[06:54] Samir: another practical tip: use small post-processing checks to detect truncated sentences (e.g., punctuation heuristics) and do a quick re-query for closure.
[07:07] Evan: let's talk integration — we use Node/Go stack. how are SDKs?
[07:11] Lucia: we have official SDKs for JS, Python, Go — streaming helpers and retry builtin. some customers use lightweight wrappers.
[07:20] Priya: is there an offline playground for QA?
[07:23] Lucia: yes sandbox + replay logs. you can run prompts offline to validate prompts and promptsets before pushing to prod.
[07:29] Darla: can Optimize detect regressions when we change prompts or models?
[07:33] Samir: yes, eval sets + quality monitoring — it will alert on regressions and tie to prompt sets.
[07:40] Evan: any integrations for ticketing systems for safety workflows?
[07:44] Lucia: we have webhooks and integrations; safety pipeline recommended for flagged outputs.
[07:50] Priya: curious about cold starts on Dedicated — if we route long requests to Dedicated, do we hit cold kernel loads?
[07:58] Lucia: initial kernel selection can add ms; we pre-warm based on traffic patterns. autoscaler warm pools help.
[08:05] Darla: ok can you summarize recommended starter config for us?
[08:09] Lucia: sure — for interactive chat with your p50 250ms target: start hosted with streaming enabled, temp 0.1, top_p 0.95, max_tokens 256, idempotency keys in requests, prefix caching for repeated prompts, and Optimize to run A/B over 1k prompt set for 7 days.
[08:27] Samir: and we recommend a small pilot run 1 week to gather real telemetry; lucia will supply benchmark script and cost sim.
[08:34] Evan: timeline — we want an internal demo next monday and pilot asap.
[08:38] Samir: we'll send availability.
[08:41] Darla: any concerns about regulatory logs?
[08:44] Samir: audit logs are available, and for strict regs recommend Private deployment. we'll include compliance matrix in the packet.
[08:52] Priya: great. a couple clarifications — can you send sample request/response with streaming headers?
[08:58] Lucia: yes, sample curl and SDK snippet will be in the follow-up.
[09:03] Evan: ok, last Q: do you support model rollbacks if we see regression?
[09:07] Samir: yes built-in rollout APIs: canary, A/B, automatic fallback to previous variant on regression. console shows rollout status and metrics.
[09:17] Darla: that's helpful. thanks everyone.
[09:20] Samir: quick recap — i'll send security docs, lucia sends bench scripts and sample code, we'll propose pilot dates. any other items?
[09:28] Evan: nope. thanks.
[09:30] Samir: thanks, we'll follow up.
